docs.summary: Provides an icon from the Nephos core with consistent size, family and accessibility, without introducing colour or artwork outside the approved set.
docs.sizeCaption: The approved sizes, with real nph-icon instances.
docs.derivedText1: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: design.md for the technical contract and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for decisions P01, P02, P03, P17, P19, P20 and P21. The nph-icon spec sheet and the DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file complete the component contract. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: A control or piece of content needs an icon that exists in the Nephos core.
The icon reinforces a label, state or direction without replacing the textual information.
whenNotToUse: The action is domain-specific or has consequences: use a text label alongside the icon.
The requested icon does not exist in the core: report the gap and wait for a decision.
The Font Awesome Pro package, files or secret in versioned material.
A visual variant created just to fill a matrix.
Duotone outside structural navigation, or Duotone and Classic mixed in the same group.
Colour defined as a property: the icon inherits currentColor from the context.
api: Required, in kebab-case and limited to the {total} icons of the Nephos core.
light by default; solid when the context needs more visual presence. Both exist for every name in the core.
sm, md or lg; free values are not accepted.
Absent or empty makes the icon decorative and applies aria-hidden. A non-empty value provides its accessible name.
Takes no focus, click or touch; the surrounding control defines the interaction.
Exposes no colour property and no initial ::part; inherits currentColor from the context.
docs.coreText: The set is Font Awesome Pro and Classic is the default family. The full catalogue, with search, is under Icons Overview, in this same folder.
docs.coreRule: light and solid exist for every name in the core; light is the default, and solid comes in when the context needs more visual presence. Never invent artwork outside the collection. Thin and Sharp are forbidden. Duotone is allowed only in structural navigation, without mixing families within one group, and has no artwork available yet.
docs.sizeText: Size is not a visual variant: it comes from a semantic token, and free values do not exist. The box is always square; the artwork is centred and scaled by height.
sizeTable: Inside a control, a table cell, a field, and next to 14px text. When in doubt, this is the one.
Menu item, tab and highlighted action, where sm looks small next to the label. Do not use inside an ordinary button.
Section heading, empty state, and an icon that carries meaning on its own. Do not use in dense screens or in lists.
docs.sizeOverflow: eye, eye-slash and star are 18 wide by nature, above the 16 of the box: the box normalises height and alignment, not width. The artwork overflows centred, without clipping and without rescaling.
docs.colorText: Colour is inherited from the context through currentColor. There is no icon colour token, and colour is not a property of the component. The gap to the text is space/inline-tight and belongs to the container that composes icon and text, not to the icon.
accessibility: With visible text beside it, the icon is decorative and takes aria-hidden — otherwise the screen reader reads it twice.
With no visible text, aria-label is required.
A meaningful icon requires 3:1 contrast (WCAG 1.4.11).
The icon is not the touch target: the target is the surrounding control, with control/height-large on touch screens.
An isolated icon takes no focus; the surrounding control defines keyboard behaviour.
Icon and colour are never the only signal of state or action.
docs.invalidText: A name outside the core, a missing size or one outside the approved list, or a variant that does not exist render no icon and fail development validation. There is no visual fallback and no free size. The error is reported through console.error in development only.
docs.invalidPointer: The cases are demonstrated under Validation › Invalid input.

badgeDocs.summary: A short tag that labels the status or the category of an item. If there is nothing to write, there is no badge.
badgeDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-badge spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P68. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: To label the status or the category of an item.
Choose the severity by meaning. A permanent status uses secondary or primary; success confirms an event that has just happened.
Write one or two words.
Turn the icon on only to reinforce the word.
Give one status per item.
whenNotToUse: As a button: the badge takes no click and no focus. Use nph-button.
success as a permanent badge: use secondary or primary.
A badge without text, with only an icon.
Two status badges on the same item.
A sentence inside the badge: supporting text stays outside the component.
Painting the background or the text by hand: the colour comes from the severity and the emphasis.
api: The severity, by meaning: primary (default), secondary, info, warn, help, danger or success. Reflected to the attribute.
The emphasis: solid (default) or light. Reflected to the attribute.
One or two words, already localized. It is the accessible name. Empty or only spaces: there is no badge.
A name from the nph-icon core, before the text. Empty: no icon.
badgeDocs.variantsCaption: The severities in the solid and light emphases; in the second row of each emphasis, with an icon.

severityUse.label: Use for a permanent state or category that needs to stand out, in the brand color.
Use for a permanent state or category, without emphasis.
Use for something the person needs to know about the item.
Use when the item asks for care before proceeding.
Use when the item has an explanation or help.
Use for a negative state of the item, such as rejected.
Use to confirm an event that has just happened, never for a permanent state.

emphasisUse.label: Use to give the badge weight.
Use to accompany the item without competing for attention.

anatomy: radius/full; space/inline-tight on top and bottom and space/control-padding on the sides. The background colour comes from the severity and the emphasis.
Before the text, at icon/size-sm, in the text colour, space/inline-tight away from it. Artwork from nph-icon.
text/label-sm, on a single line. It is the accessible name of the component.
accessibility: Contrast
The text passes 4.5:1 in every severity and emphasis, in both modes and in every brand; the lowest value is 4.64:1, in primary light in light mode.
Visible focus
The badge takes no click and no focus. For an action, use nph-button.
Colour is not the only signal
Every badge has text: colour is never the only signal, and the icon only reinforces the word.
Touch target
It is not a touch target: the badge takes no click.
Accessible name
The text is the accessible name of the component. The icon is decorative.

buttonDocs.summary: Triggers an action identified by text. It varies in severity, emphasis, size and state, with an optional icon at the start or the end. Without text, it is the icon-only button.
buttonDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-button spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P68. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: To start an action identified by text, such as save or send.
Write in the text what happens on click.
Choose the severity by the meaning of the action, never by colour.
Choose the emphasis by how much the action stands out: solid, outline, light or ghost.
Use size large on touch screens.
Without text, use the icon-only button and give it an accessible name.
whenNotToUse: To show a field error: validation belongs to the field (nph-field).
Icon only on an action with consequences, such as delete or publish.
To navigate to another destination.
size compact as the main target on a touch screen.
Enlarging the icon to add emphasis.
Using colour as the only signal of intent, focus or state.
Creating a severity, emphasis or size outside the matrix, or painting the button by hand.
api: The severity, by the meaning of the action: primary (default), secondary, info, warn, help, danger or success. Reflected to the attribute.
How much the action stands out: solid (default), outline, light or ghost. outline, light and ghost exist only in primary, secondary and danger. Reflected to the attribute.
compact, default (the default) or large. large meets the 44 px touch target. Reflected to the attribute.
What happens on click, already localized. It is the accessible name.
A name from the nph-icon core before the text, at icon/size-sm. It can coexist with icon-end.
A name from the nph-icon core after the text, at icon/size-sm.
Accessible name of the button without text. Required there; with text, it is not used.
Turns the button off: it leaves the Tab order and fires no click. Reflected to the attribute.
Shows the nph-spinner in place of the start icon; the text stays, focus remains and the click does not reach the consumer. Reflected to the attribute.
buttonDocs.variantsCaption: The severities in each emphasis, at the default size. Hover to see the hover state and use Tab to see focus.
buttonDocs.severityNote: info, warn, help and success exist only in solid.

severityUse.label: Use for the main action of the block.
Use for the alternative action that accompanies the main one, such as Cancel next to Save.
Use for an action that deletes, revokes or cannot be undone.
Use for an action tied to neutral information, such as a system notice or a contextual tip.
Use for an action that requires care before proceeding.
Use for an action that opens help or guidance, such as an explanation, a tour or support content.
Use for an action that confirms something succeeded.

severityDont.label: Do not use next to another primary solid action in the same block.
Do not use as the only main action of the block.
Do not use with an icon only: write the text.
Do not use for an error, a risk or a confirmation.
Do not use for an error that has already happened; for an action that deletes or cannot be undone, use danger.
Do not use to report a system state.
Do not use to label a permanent state, such as active: use nph-badge.

buttonDocs.sizesText: The height comes from control/height-compact, -default or -large. The text is text/label-md in all of them. Without text, the button is square and the icon follows the box: sm in compact, md in default and lg in large.
buttonDocs.sizesCaption: compact, default and large, with text, with an icon and icon only.

sizeUse.label: Use inside a table, toolbar or filter.
Use everywhere else; it is the default.
Use on a touch screen and in the main form; it meets the 44 px touch target.

sizeDont.label: Do not use as the main target on a touch screen, or with a different size from the field beside it.
Do not use with a different size from the field beside it.
Do not use with a different size from the field beside it.

states: default
Rest. The colour conveys the severity of the action.
hover-active
The surface changes to the hover token of the severity and emphasis.
focus
For keyboard users: a border in the severity colour and a halo outside it, without changing the size. In secondary, the border is focus/border.
disabled
The whole button at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order.
loading
The nph-spinner in place of the start icon. The text stays.
accessibility: Contrast
Text and icon pass 4.5:1 in every severity and emphasis, in both modes and in every brand; the lowest value is 4.64:1, in primary outline and light in light mode. Borders pass 3:1.
Visible focus
On focus, the border and the halo appear for keyboard users.
Colour is not the only signal
Colour is never the only signal of intent, focus or state: the text says what happens on click.
Touch target
size large meets the 44 px touch target; compact is not a main target on a touch screen.
Accessible name
The text is the name of the button. Without text, the name comes from label, which is required.
Keyboard
Tab moves in and out; Enter and Space activate.

buttonDocs.exampleIconOnly: A universal action without text, with an accessible name.

labelDocs.summary: Tells people what they need to type or choose in a field. It can mark the field as required and show an information icon. The text has no state; only the information icon takes focus.
labelDocs.derivedText: If anything differs, the canonical sources win: the nph-label spec, design.md for tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P62. The Figma file DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 is the visual source. No rule is created here.
labelDocs.info: Explains what the field asks for.
labelDocs.description: Use nph-label to give a form control a visible name, on its own or inside an nph-field. The label is just text: it has no state, size or layout. The exception is the information icon, which takes focus. It does not replace the section title, which is heading-sm, body text, or help and error messages, which belong to nph-field.
anatomy: marks the field as required, in status/error
accessibility: contrast

The text uses color/foreground: 21:1 in light and 14.73:1 in dark, above 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3). The asterisk, in status/error, has 6.88:1 and 5.01:1. The information icon, in color/muted-foreground, has 6.69:1 and 9.81:1, and the focus border, in focus/border, 3.68:1 and 8.98:1, above 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11).
visible focus

The label text does not take focus: focus shows on the control it names. The information icon is a trigger and, when focused, shows the focus/border border and the focus/halo halo around the target (state=focus).
colour is not the only cue
Required is marked by the asterisk, explained in a visible legend on the form. The label does not use color/destructive, which mixes up required and error.
touch target
The information icon has a 24×24 target, with the 16 px art in the centre (WCAG 2.5.8). Clicking the label text moves focus to the control it names.
accessible name
The label text is the visible name of the control it goes with.
labelDocs.accessibilityCaption: The text is the visible name of the control. Required marked by the asterisk. Information icon after the text.
properties: variant · default false. Values: false · true. true when filling in the field is mandatory: adds the asterisk after the text. false carries no indicator.
variant · default false. Values: false · true. true adds the information icon after the text. In code, info is the explanation text: when set, it shows the icon.
variant · default default. Values: default · focus. focus only exists with info=true and shows the focus of the information icon. The label text has no state.
api: Boolean, default false. Reflects to the attribute.
The id of the control the label names, as in the native <label>. Reflects to the attribute.

The explanation text, already localized. With info-label, it shows the information icon, which opens nph-tooltip with this text on hover and on keyboard focus, above the label, and closes with Esc, when the pointer leaves or on blur.
The accessible name of the information icon. Without it, the icon does not appear.
relations: Inside an nph-field, the label is the field's own; do not add a loose nph-label next to it.
Help and error messages belong to nph-field, not to the label.
The space to the control is space/stack-tight.
The label stays in color/foreground even when the field has an error: the field shows the error.
The information icon opens nph-tooltip, which shows the info text above the label.
labelDocs.relationsCaption: On its own, above the control, with space/stack-tight.
whenToUse: To give a form control a visible name, on its own or inside an nph-field.
required=true when filling in the field is mandatory, with the asterisk explained in a legend on the form.
info=true to show the information icon after the text.
Explain the asterisk in a visible legend on the form.
Keep the label in color/foreground, even when the field has an error.
examplesCaptions: Required field: the asterisk comes from required.
Label on its own, above the control.
dont: Using it for a sentence with a verb and a full stop: that is body text.
Using it as a section or group title: that is heading-sm.
Using it for emphasis inside a paragraph: that is <strong>.
Putting help or an error message in the label: they belong to nph-field.
Using the field's example text instead of the label.
Painting the label or the asterisk with color/destructive: it mixes up required and error.

labelValidation.info: Explains what the field asks for.
labelValidation.matrixCaption: required adds the asterisk; info with info-label adds the information icon.
labelValidation.associationCaption: Click the label: the cursor moves to the field.
labelValidation.errorTitle: An error does not change the label
labelValidation.errorCaption: The label stays in color/foreground. The error shows on the field and in the message below it — never on the label.
labelValidation.disabledTitle: Disabled is not a label state
labelValidation.disabledCaption: nph-field will apply state/disabled-opacity to the whole control. The label has no state of its own.
labelValidation.focusCaption: Click the field and press Tab: focus moves to the information icon. The label text does not take focus. The balloon opens with the focus.
labelValidation.openCaption: The balloon opens above the label when the pointer rests on the icon or the icon receives keyboard focus, and closes with Esc, when the pointer leaves or on blur. It does not open on touch.

tooltipValidation.oneLine: Explains what the field asks for.
tooltipValidation.twoLines: Use the name as it appears on the document, without abbreviating.
tooltipValidation.sidesCaption: Top is the default; the balloon flips to the opposite side when it does not fit, and may also sit bottom, left or right. The distance to the element is space/inline.
tooltipValidation.flipCaption: The element sits at the top of the window: the balloon prefers top, does not fit and sits below.
tooltipValidation.focusCaption: Press Tab to focus the button: the balloon opens and the focus stays on the button. Press Esc to close it.
tooltipValidation.hoverCaption: Put the pointer on each element, or focus it with Tab: the balloon opens at once, on any element. It stays open while the pointer is over it.

tooltipDocs.summary: A floating text balloon attached to any element of the interface. It shows complementary information, an explanation or context data when the pointer rests on the element and when the element receives keyboard focus.
tooltipDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-tooltip spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P77. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
tooltipDocs.description: Use nph-tooltip to give complementary information, an explanation or context data to any element, such as the icon-only button and the information icon of the nph-label. The balloon opens on hover and on focus, with no delay, and closes when the pointer leaves the element and the balloon, on blur or with Esc. It does not replace the help text or the error message, which belong to nph-field, nor the accessible name of the element.
whenToUse: To give the action name to every icon-only button.
For complementary information or context data of any element.
For one sentence the person reads at once, before filling in.
whenNotToUse: To put an action, a link or a field inside the balloon: use nph-popover.
To repeat in the balloon the help text of the field: that belongs to nph-field.
To put in the balloon information without which the element cannot be used.
To cut the text with an ellipsis or let it pass two lines: rewrite until it fits.
api: The balloon content, already localized by the application, with no action and no link. The balloon follows the text up to layout/max-tooltip-width and wraps; it fits at most two lines. The text must fit whole: no ellipsis and no broken word.

The id of the element that opens the balloon, in the same root as the tooltip, as in the native label. The tooltip listens on that element and adds its own id to the aria-describedby of the element. Without a matching element, nothing is drawn.
The preferred side: top (default), bottom, left or right. The balloon flips to the opposite side when it does not fit. It is behavior: the Figma component has no side property.
Boolean, reflected to the attribute. The tooltip turns it on and off by itself; the consumer may turn it on to show the balloon open, and the same closing rules apply.
relations: The balloon opens from any element: the icon-only button carries the action name; the information icon of the nph-label carries the explanation.
The balloon text comes from the element that opens it; on the nph-label, from the info property.
Help text and error message stay in nph-field, not in the balloon.
The balloon sits next to the element, at space/inline, without covering its focus.
tooltipDocs.relationsCaption: Opened from the information icon of the nph-label, above the label.
anatomy: Background color/tooltip, corners radius/inner, shadow elevation/dropdown, padding space/inline (left and right) and space/inline-tight (top and bottom); at most layout/max-tooltip-width wide and layout/max-tooltip-height tall. It enters on motion/enter-duration and leaves on motion/exit-duration.
space/inline, so the balloon does not cover the focus of the element. Top by default; flips when it does not fit; may also sit bottom, left or right.
accessibility: Semantics
The host is role=tooltip from mount, and the element it describes points to it with aria-describedby. The balloon is rendered always and shown only when open.
Contrast
The text uses color/tooltip-foreground on color/tooltip: 6.69:1 in light and 7.47:1 in dark, above 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3).
Visible focus
The balloon never takes focus: focus stays on the element that opened it, with that element's focus drawing. The balloon stays open while the pointer is over it (WCAG 1.4.13).
Keyboard
Keyboard focus on the element opens the balloon; Esc closes it. Hover also opens it.
Touch target
The balloon is not a touch target and does not open on touch: without hover, essential information never lives only in the balloon. The touch target is the element, at its own size (WCAG 2.5.8).
Accessible name
The balloon complements the element's accessible name and does not replace it: on the icon-only button, the action name stays on the button itself.

skeletonDocs.summary: A still shape that holds the place of a content while it loads. It repeats the shape of what will come in — text, image or person — and does not pulse.
skeletonDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-skeleton spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P69. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: When the shape of the content is known and it is still loading.
Choose the shape equal to the content: line for text, block for an image or area, avatar for a person.
Repeat the shape of the final content, because the swap must not move the layout.
Use the avatar shape in the size of the nph-avatar that will come in, because the size stays the same.
Announce the wait on the container, because the shape is not read.
Keep the piece still, because it has no pulse.
whenNotToUse: When the shape of the content is not known: use nph-spinner.
When there is no content, or as an empty state: use nph-empty.
One avatar size in place of another: use the avatar shape of the same size.
api: The shape of the place: line (default), block, avatar-sm, avatar-md or avatar-lg. It is the Figma property forma. Reflected to the attribute.
Not properties: the line and the block stretch to the container width, and the block height follows the content that will come in, so the consumer gives it.
Does not exist: the piece is still.
Not a property: the shape always uses color/muted.
skeletonDocs.shapesCaption: The five shapes of the set: line, block and the avatar in the three sizes.

shapesUse.label: The place of a text line. It takes its own skeleton/line-height; the space between lines comes from the consumer.
The place of an image, chart or area. The width comes from the container and the height follows the content that will come in.
The place of an nph-avatar sm, with avatar/size-sm.
The place of an nph-avatar md, with avatar/size-md.
The place of an nph-avatar lg, with avatar/size-lg.

relations: It builds the place of other pieces: avatar and lines in place of a person, lines in place of a paragraph, a block in place of an image.
The avatar shape uses avatar/size-* and avatar/radius-*, like nph-avatar.
Between shapes, the space is the same as the content that will come in.
When the content arrives, it enters the exact place of the shape.
anatomy: A rectangle in color/muted, with no border, no text and no animation.
radius/inner on the line, radius/control on the block and avatar/radius-* on the avatar, with rounded corners, never a circle.
The avatar in avatar/size-*; the line height in skeleton/line-height. The width of the line and the block comes from the container, and the block height follows the content that will come in.
accessibility: Contrast
The shape carries no information: the contrast with the background is low on purpose and does not need to reach 3:1. The loading information comes from the container.
Visible focus
The piece does not receive focus.
Color is not the only signal
The wait is announced by the container, not by the color of the shape.
Touch target
It is not interactive and has no touch target.
Accessible name
The shape gets aria-hidden; the loading container gets aria-busy while it waits.
Motion
The piece is still: there is no pulse to reduce when the person prefers less motion.

skeletonDocs.exampleCard: Card loading: a block in place of the image and lines in place of the text.
skeletonDocs.exampleParagraph: Paragraph loading: one line per text line.

togglebuttonDocs.summary: A button that holds a boolean value, on or off, and shows the state in the piece itself: the inner area rises, with a shadow and an outline. It takes text or an icon only, and fires nph-change when the person toggles it.
togglebuttonDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-togglebutton spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P73. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: In a toolbar, when the option turns on or off with an immediate effect, among other buttons.
With text, when the option name must be visible.
Icon only, when the icon is recognized without a caption: give it an accessible name.
Start and end icons are optional: the raised inner area with an outline still shows the state.
whenNotToUse: To fire an action: use nph-button.
Outside a toolbar, in a setting that turns on or off with an immediate effect: use nph-switch.
In a form, when the choice goes with the submission: use nph-checkbox.
To mark the state by changing only the text color: turn pressed on.
togglebuttonDocs.relationsText: It does not replace nph-button: nph-button fires an action and nph-togglebutton holds a state. nph-toggle-group exists: it is a set of these pieces, separated by space/inline. nph-switch (a setting outside a toolbar) and nph-checkbox (a choice in a form) are planned and do not exist yet.
api: The on state, the Figma property marcado. false by default. Reflected to the attribute. A click, Enter or Space by the person toggles it and fires nph-change; setting it from code never fires the event.
The border of the track becomes status/error, and on focus the halo becomes focus/halo-error. Reflected to the attribute. The error message stays outside the piece. disabled wins over it.
Turns the piece off: it leaves the Tab order, does not toggle, does not fire nph-change and stays at state/disabled-opacity. Reflected to the attribute.
The option name, already localized. It is the accessible name and stays on one line. Without it, the piece is icon only and needs label.
Accessible name of the icon-only piece. Required there; with text, it is not used.
auto (default), none or a name from the nph-icon core, before the text, at icon/size-sm. auto is xmark when off and check when on. A name is one fixed icon. Icon only uses this one.
The same values, after the text. Icon only ignores it.
The event fired when the person toggles the piece. It bubbles, crosses the shadow root and is not cancelable. detail.pressed carries the new value.
states: unpressed
The track and the inner area share color/muted; the label and the icon use color/muted-foreground.
pressed
The inner area rises, with color/background, elevation/subtle and an outline in color/primary-border. The label and the icon use color/foreground, and the icon changes from xmark to check.
hover
In the unpressed piece, the label and the icon go from color/muted-foreground to color/foreground.
focus
For keyboard users: a border in color/primary and a halo in focus/halo outside the piece, without changing the size.
invalid
The border of the track becomes status/error; on focus, the border and the halo are status/error and focus/halo-error. The error message stays outside the piece.
disabled
The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order. It wins over invalid: the error border is not drawn.
togglebuttonDocs.statesCaption: unpressed, pressed, invalid, disabled and disabled with invalid. Move the mouse over a button to see hover and press Tab to see focus.
togglebuttonDocs.iconsText: Each side takes auto, none or a name from the nph-icon core. Icon only draws the icon of icon-start alone.
togglebuttonDocs.iconsCaption: Each row is off and on: the auto pair, no icon, one fixed icon, start only, end only and icon only.
icons: The default. xmark when off and check when on, both rendered and cross-faded by opacity.
No icon on that side. Icon only with icon-start none has nothing to draw: the piece renders nothing.
Any name from the nph-icon core, such as star: one fixed icon, with no swap.
anatomy: The outer box: background color/muted, border border/width in color/muted, radius/control, height control/height-default and space/inline-tight of padding on the four sides. When invalid, the border is status/error.

Holds the content: radius/inner, side padding space/control-padding and space/inline-tight between icon and label. When pressed: color/background, elevation/subtle and an outline in color/primary-border at border/width.
Optional, at icon/size-sm. By default xmark when off and check when on.
The text, in text/label-md: color/muted-foreground when off; color/foreground when pressed or on hover.
Optional, with the same values and the same swap as the start icon.
A border in color/primary and a halo in focus/halo outside the piece; when invalid, status/error and focus/halo-error.
accessibility: Semantics
A native button with type=button and aria-pressed following pressed. Never role switch or aria-checked. aria-invalid is not valid on a button: invalid is shown by the border.
Accessible name
The visible text. Icon only, label is required and becomes the aria-label of the button; the icons are aria-hidden.
Keyboard
Tab enters and leaves; Enter and Space toggle.
Visible focus
Keyboard only: a border and a halo outside the piece, without changing the size.
Contrast

The off label, color/muted-foreground on color/muted, passes 4.5:1: 5.76:1 in light and 6.61:1 in dark. The outline of the pressed inner area, color/primary-border on the track, passes 3:1 in every brand and in both modes; the lowest value is 3.31:1, in dark gerencial. The error border, status/error on color/background, is 6.88:1 in light and 5.01:1 in dark.
Known limit

In dark mode, the focus border color/primary is below 3:1 against the page background in gerencial (2.71:1) and rh (2.88:1), and against the halo in every brand (1.76:1 to 2.94:1). In light mode both pass, and the lowest value is 3.33:1 against the halo, in educacao. design.md says only focus/border guarantees 3:1; this piece uses color/primary, as the accepted frame says.
Color is not the only signal
The pressed state shows in the raised inner area with an outline and in the icon, not only in the text color. The invalid piece changes its border; the error message stays outside.
Touch target
The whole piece is the target: 36 px high, with or without text. Icon only is 50 by 36 px.
Motion
The change animates on motion/state-duration and motion/state-easing; under reduced motion it takes motion/hover-duration, and the color still changes.
togglebuttonDocs.exampleOn: Option on: on, with text and icons.
togglebuttonDocs.exampleIconSet: Icon set: icon only, side by side, one on.

toggleGroupDocs.summary: A group of nph-togglebutton on the same subject, side by side in a toolbar and separated by space/inline. The group gathers and spaces the buttons and coordinates the selection, single or multiple; it adds no color, border or focus of its own.
toggleGroupDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-toggle-group spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P76. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: When two or more options on the same subject stay together in the toolbar.
With text, when the icon alone does not say the option; icon only, when the icon is known and each button has a label.
Single selection when the options exclude each other, such as alignment; multiple when they add up, such as bold and italic.
whenNotToUse: To fire actions: use nph-button.
For a single option: use nph-togglebutton, without a group.
To join the buttons without space: nph-toggle-group already brings space/inline.
To mix buttons with text and icon-only buttons in the same group: choose one.
Outside a toolbar, in a setting that turns on or off with an immediate effect: use nph-switch.
In a form, when the choice goes with the submission: use nph-checkbox.
toggleGroupDocs.relationsText: The group is made of nph-togglebutton, which keeps its own color, state and focus: the group only gathers the buttons, spaces them with space/inline and coordinates the selection. It sits in a toolbar, next to other buttons. nph-switch and nph-checkbox are planned and do not exist yet. When a button is invalid, the error message stays outside the group.
api: The name of the group, the subject: Alignment, Formatting. Required: it becomes the aria-label of the host, which is the group. A name the consumer puts on the host with aria-label or aria-labelledby also counts.
single (default) or multiple. It is behavior, not appearance: in single, checking a button unchecks the others and one stays checked once a choice is made; in multiple, each button is free.

The checked buttons, by the value of each. The attribute takes words separated by spaces, value="bold italic"; the property is a list of strings. Single holds zero or one. With no value, none is checked. The group writes pressed on every button from it. Setting it from code never fires the event.
Each nph-togglebutton in the group names itself with a value attribute. The group reads it and the button ignores it. It must be a word with no space, and unique in the group.
The nph-togglebutton buttons: at least two, with no maximum. Text, label, icons, disabled and invalid stay on each button.

The event fired when the person changes the selection. It bubbles, crosses the shadow root and is not cancelable. detail.value is the list of checked values, in the order of the buttons. The nph-change of each button is not stopped.
toggleGroupDocs.selectionText: The Figma frame leaves single and multiple selection to code: it is behavior, not appearance. The group coordinates it, so each button no longer decides alone.
toggleGroupDocs.selectionCaption: Single with no value, single with a value, multiple with no value and multiple with two values checked.
selectionRules: Checks it, unchecks the others and fires nph-value-change with one value.
Nothing: the button stays checked, no event fires and the click does not reach the page. One button is always checked once a choice is made.
None is checked until the first click.
Each click checks or unchecks that button; the value gathers the checked ones, in the order of the buttons.
Setting value moves the checks and never fires the event. The group is the source of truth: a pressed attribute on a button is overwritten.
With fewer than two buttons the group still renders and logs a warning in development. Mixing buttons with text and icon-only buttons logs a warning too.
anatomy: The host, a row with space/inline between the buttons. No background, border, outline or focus of its own. With invalid input, it takes no space.
An nph-togglebutton, with its own state: pressed, focus, disabled and invalid. 36 px high, control/height-default.
space/inline (8 px) between neighbors: the buttons are never joined, and the space avoids the wrong touch.
accessibility: Semantics

The host is role=group, named by label. Each button is a native button with aria-pressed (nph-togglebutton). Single selection is not a radio group: the screen reader reads the state of each button and does not announce that the choice is exclusive.
Accessible name
The group is named with the subject (label). Each icon-only button gets its own label.
Keyboard
One Tab stop per button, in order; a disabled button is skipped. Enter and Space toggle. There are no arrow keys: a roving tabindex across groups belongs to a toolbar.
Visible focus
Each button shows its own focus, as nph-togglebutton does. The group does not receive focus.
Contrast
It comes from nph-togglebutton, on its own background in both modes. The group adds no color.
Color is not the only signal
The pressed button changes its inner area (background, shadow and outline), not only the text color.
Touch target
Each button is control/height-default high, and neighbors are space/inline apart.
Known limit
The focus border of nph-togglebutton, color/primary, is below 3:1 in dark mode in some brands, as the nph-togglebutton page documents. The group does not change it.

avatarDocs.summary: The picture of a person: the photo, or the person icon when there is none. A square with rounded corners, in three sizes, with a border drawn over the photo. It shows who the person is next to the name; it is not a button and it opens nothing.
avatarDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-avatar spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P74. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: Next to a person's name, when the person needs to be recognized in a list, a field or a header.
sm next to body text, in a list and in the select; md in a header, card and table row; lg in a profile.
Without a photo, keep the avatar: it draws the person icon whenever there is no src or the image does not load.
Put the person's name next to it: the avatar alone does not identify anyone with certainty.
Use the same size for every avatar in a list.
whenNotToUse: As a button: the avatar receives no click and no focus.
As an action icon: use nph-icon.
As a circle: the avatar is a square with rounded corners, and there is no shape property.
With an empty frame: leave src out and the person icon shows.
avatarDocs.relationsText: It goes next to the person's name, set apart by space/inline. nph-avatar-stack overlaps a group of avatars, with the count of who does not show. nph-select will take it at the start of the trigger and of each option, in size sm; it is planned and does not exist yet. nph-icon is the piece for an action icon and draws the person icon inside the avatar; nph-skeleton is the placeholder for a list while its data loads.
api: sm (default), md or lg: the Figma size. Reflected to the attribute. The frame is 24, 32 or 40 px, a square with avatar/radius-*, never a circle. An invalid value renders nothing and logs one console.error in development.

The address of the photo. There is no tipo property in code: it derives from src. With src, the piece is foto; without it, sem foto. Empty or whitespace-only counts as none. The photo takes the place of the icon when it loads, and a new src starts the wait again. No event is emitted.
The accessible name. With text, the host takes role=img and aria-label. Empty or whitespace-only, the avatar is decorative: aria-hidden=true on the host. No label is valid and silent.
None. The avatar has no slot, no ::part, no event, no initials and no form association.
avatarDocs.fallbackText: The frame is never empty. Without a photo, the person icon shows: nph-icon user, style light, at the icon/size-* of the avatar size. The Figma tipo defaults to foto, but in code there is no tipo: it derives from src, so <nph-avatar> with no attribute draws sem foto.
avatarDocs.fallbackCaption: A photo, no src and a src that fails, at size lg. The last two draw the same person icon.
fallback: The person icon (sem foto). It is the default of <nph-avatar>.
The person icon, as in sem foto. The photo takes its place on load.
The photo fills the frame and crops to keep its proportion; the icon leaves. The border stays over the photo.
The person icon stays. No event and no error are emitted. A new src starts the wait again.
The same as no src: no image is rendered.
anatomy: A square of avatar/size-sm, -md or -lg (24, 32 and 40 px), with avatar/radius-* and color/muted as background. It clips its content and never shrinks, so a group sums up exactly.
The image of src, with an empty alt: the name belongs to the host. It fills the frame and crops to keep its proportion. It has no border of its own.
nph-icon user, style light, in color/muted-foreground, centered, at icon/size-sm, -md or -lg by the avatar size.
border/width in color/border, drawn by the avatar inside the frame and over the photo, with the corner of the frame. It keeps overlapped avatars apart; there is no property for it.
accessibility: Semantics
An image on the host, or nothing: aria-hidden=true by default, role=img with aria-label when label has text. It is never focusable and it is not a button.
Accessible name
With the name next to it, leave label out: the avatar is hidden from the screen reader. Alone, pass label with the person's name and it announces it. The inner image has an empty alt.
Visible focus
Not applicable: the avatar does not receive focus. Inside a control, the focus belongs to the control.
Contrast

The person icon, color/muted-foreground on color/muted, passes 3:1 in light and dark, in every brand; nph-avatar.test.ts measures it by hand until the accessibility gate (P72, DSA-32) arrives. The photo is the person's image and is not measured.
Color is not the only signal
The avatar does not communicate state.
Touch target
Not applicable: the avatar is not interactive. The target is the one of the control that contains it.
Motion
None: the avatar has no animation and no transition.
avatarDocs.exampleOwner: Owner select: the avatar at size sm with the name next to it, set apart by space/inline. It is a row built for this page, not the select: nph-select does not exist yet.
avatarDocs.exampleCard: Card header: the avatar at size md with the name and a role line, in a row built for this page.
avatarDocs.exampleProfile: Profile without photo: size lg with no src, so the person icon shows.

avatarStackDocs.summary: A group of overlapping avatars that shows several people in a short space, with the count of who does not show. Each avatar is an nph-avatar; the group is read as one image, by its name.
avatarStackDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-avatar-stack spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P78. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: To show who takes part in something, such as owners, members or participants, without listing everyone.
Show up to the 5th avatar; whoever does not show enters the count.
Turn on the count when there are more people than avatars, because the total must show.
sm in a list and in the select; md in a header, card and table row; lg in a profile.
Give the group a label with the names and the total, because the avatars are not read.
whenNotToUse: For a single person: use nph-avatar.
As the list of people with their names: the group does not replace it.
To space avatars without overlap: nph-avatar-stack already brings avatar/overlap.
To mix sizes in the group: the group has a single size and writes it on every avatar.
Past the 5th avatar: put whoever does not show in the count.
avatarStackDocs.relationsText: Each avatar is an nph-avatar, with its own photo or the person icon; its border, drawn over the photo, is what keeps the overlapped avatars apart. The overlap is avatar/overlap, which belongs to this piece only. Next to a text, such as the team name, the space is space/inline and is given by whoever uses the group.
api: sm (default), md or lg: the Figma size, the same sizes as nph-avatar. Reflected to the attribute. The group writes it on every child avatar, also when a child changes its own. An invalid value renders nothing and logs one console.error in development.

How many people do not show: the Figma mostrar contagem and contagem. A whole number; above zero the group draws +N at the end. Zero or no attribute draws no count. A negative or broken number renders nothing and logs one console.error in development.

The name of the group, already localized, with the names and the total, such as Ana, Bruno, Carla and 3 more. It becomes the aria-label of the host. aria-label or aria-labelledby on the host also count. No name renders nothing and logs one console.error in development.
The nph-avatar children, from the 2nd to the 5th, each with its own src. The Figma mostrar 3º, mostrar 4º and mostrar 5º are the number of children, not properties.
None. The group has no ::part, no event, no color property and no form association.
avatarStackDocs.compositionText: The 1st and the 2nd avatars are always there; the 3rd to the 5th are added as children. Whoever does not show enters the count, at the end of the group, overlapping the last avatar like any neighbor. The count does not check the name: label and count are written together by whoever uses the group.
avatarStackDocs.compositionCaption: Two avatars, five avatars, and five avatars with the count, at size md.
composition: Draws them in a row, each over the previous one by avatar/overlap.
Draws +N after the last avatar, growing with the number.
Fewer than 2 or more than 5 avatars
Draws all of them and warns in development: for one person, use nph-avatar; past the 5th, use the count.
A child that is not an nph-avatar
It is not part of the group, and the group warns in development.
An avatar with a label of its own
The group still reads only its own name, and warns in development: put the names in the label of the group.
anatomy: An nph-avatar in the size of the group. Photo, person icon, corner and border come from it.
avatar/overlap between neighbors: each avatar goes over the previous one, and the count goes over the last avatar.

A box of avatar/size-* high and at least as wide, with avatar/radius-*, side padding space/inline-tight, background color/muted and a border/width border in color/border, inside. The +N text is color/muted-foreground, in text/label-sm in sm and md and text/label-md in lg.
The border of each nph-avatar. The group draws no ring, background or border of its own.
accessibility: Semantics
The host is one image, role=img, named by label. The avatars and the count are inside a hidden wrapper, so they are not read, even an avatar with a label of its own.
Accessible name
The names and the total, such as Ana, Bruno, Carla and 3 more, written by whoever uses the group, in its language.
Visible focus
Not applicable: the group does not receive focus. When the group opens the list of people, the focus belongs to the control around it.
Contrast
The +N text, color/muted-foreground on color/muted, passes 4.5:1 in light and dark, in every brand; nph-avatar-stack.test.ts measures it by hand until the accessibility gate (P72, DSA-32) arrives.
Color is not the only signal
Each person shows by photo or person icon, and the total shows as text.
Touch target
Not applicable: the group is not interactive.
Motion
None: the group has no animation and no transition.

switchDocs.summary: A switch that turns a setting on or off, with an immediate effect. The position of the knob shows the state: left, off; right, on. The label sits after the track, and the piece fires the native input and change when the person toggles it.
switchDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-switch spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P79. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: For a setting that turns on or off, with an immediate effect, outside a toolbar.
Several settings stack, one nph-switch per line: there is no group component.
Without text only when the name is already in the context, such as a table cell, always with label.
whenNotToUse: In a form, when the choice only counts on submission: use nph-checkbox.
In a toolbar, among other buttons: use nph-togglebutton.
To paint the track or the knob by hand: use checked, invalid and disabled.
To hide the label by deleting its text: leave text empty and give label.
switchDocs.relationsText: In a toolbar, among other buttons, the piece is nph-togglebutton; in a form whose choice only counts on submission, it is nph-checkbox. The piece brings its own text: it does not need nph-field to have a name. Inside nph-field, it is one option of a group.
api: The on state, the Figma property marcado. false by default. Reflected to the attribute. A click, Enter or Space by the person toggles it and fires input and change; setting it from code fires nothing.

The label, already localized, after the track. It is the accessible name and wraps to the available width. Without it (the Figma boolean that shows the label, off), the piece is only the track and needs label.
Accessible name of the piece without text. Required there; with text, it is not used.

The track outline becomes status/error, on or off, and on focus the halo becomes focus/halo-error. Reflected to the attribute; it sets aria-invalid. The error sentence stays outside the piece. disabled wins over it.
Turns the piece off: it leaves the Tab order, does not toggle, fires nothing and stays at state/disabled-opacity. Reflected to the attribute.
The native events, fired in this order when the person toggles the piece. input bubbles and crosses shadow roots; change bubbles and does not. The new value is read from event.target.checked.
states: off
The track is color/input, with no outline; the knob is color/background, on the left.
on
The track is color/primary, with an outline in color/primary-border drawn inside it; the knob is color/primary-foreground, on the right.
hover
Over the whole piece, the fill goes to color/input-hover when off and color/primary-hover when on; the outline stays.
focus
For keyboard users: the track outline turns focus/border and a halo in focus/halo shows outside the track, both fully rounded, without changing the size.
invalid
The track outline is status/error, on or off; on focus, the halo is focus/halo-error. The error sentence stays outside the piece.
disabled
The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order; on keeps its outline. It wins over invalid: the error outline is not drawn.
switchDocs.statesCaption: off, on, invalid, disabled and disabled with invalid. Move the mouse over a piece to see hover and press Tab to see focus.
switchDocs.labelText: The label sits after the track, space/inline from it, in text/label-md and color/foreground. It wraps to the available width; with two lines, the track sits at the top, aligned with the first line. Without text the piece is only the track, and label gives it a name.
switchDocs.labelCaption: With a label, only the track with label, and a long label on two lines.
anatomy: The rounded base, radius/full, switch/track-width by icon/size-lg. Off: color/input, no outline. On: color/primary, with an outline border/width in color/primary-border drawn inside. Hover: color/input-hover or color/primary-hover. Invalid: outline status/error.
The circle in icon/size-sm, space/inline-tight from the track edge. Off: on the left, in color/background. On: on the right, in color/primary-foreground. It slides by transform.
The text after the track, in text/label-md and color/foreground, space/inline from the track. It is the name of the control.
The whole track, switch/track-width by icon/size-lg; with a label, the whole piece.
The track outline turns focus/border and a halo focus/ring-width in focus/halo shows outside the track, both radius/full; with an error, status/error and focus/halo-error.
accessibility: Semantics
A native button with type=button, role=switch and aria-checked following checked; the track is aria-hidden. invalid sets aria-invalid. The piece is not associated with a form.
Accessible name
The label text. Without text, label is required and becomes the aria-label of the button.
Keyboard
Tab enters and leaves; Space and Enter toggle.
Visible focus
Keyboard only: the focus outline and the halo around the track, without changing the size.
Contrast

The track edge passes 3:1 on the page background: color/input is 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark; color/primary-border is at least 4.96:1 in light and 4.91:1 in dark, in every brand. The knob passes 3:1 on its track: color/background on color/input is 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark; color/primary-foreground on color/primary is at least 4.96:1. The error outline, status/error, is 6.88:1 in light and 5.01:1 in dark.
Known limit

focus/border against focus/halo is below 3:1 only in the default brand in light mode, at 2.92:1, as design.md records; in every other brand and scheme it passes. A forced-colors mode and a right-to-left page are not handled yet. The error sentence outside the piece cannot be tied to it by aria-describedby across the shadow root.
Color is not the only signal
On and off show in the knob position, not only in the track color. The error has its sentence written outside the piece.
Touch target
The whole track, 40 by 24 px; with a label, the whole piece.
Motion

The knob slides and the colors change on motion/state-duration and motion/state-easing. Under reduced motion the knob does not slide: it changes side by opacity, on motion/hover-duration, and the color still changes.
switchDocs.exampleSingle: Single setting: one option that turns on or off, with an immediate effect.
switchDocs.examplePreferences: Preferences: several settings stacked, one per line.
switchDocs.exampleUnavailable: Unavailable setting: disabled, the person cannot change it.

claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--sizes: The three sizes, with a photo and without: a square of 24, 32 and 40 px with a rounded corner, never a circle.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--photo: A valid src fills the frame and replaces the person icon; the border stays over the picture.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--no-pho: Without src, or with an empty one, the person icon shows at the icon size of each avatar size.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--photo-: A src that does not load keeps the person icon, with no event and no error.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--border: The avatar draws its own border over the photo: overlapped by hand, with a negative margin on a plain wrapper, the neighbors stay separated. The group itself is nph-avatar-stack, which uses the same border.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--access: With label the avatar is an image named by it; without label it is hidden from the screen reader and the name beside it speaks.
claims.components-nph-avatar-stack-validation--: The three sizes, without and with the count: the group writes its size on every avatar, overlaps them by avatar/overlap and draws the count in the same size.
Two to five avatars, with and without the count: what the Figma mostrar 3º, mostrar 4º, mostrar 5º and mostrar contagem turn on.
Photos and no photo in the same group: each avatar keeps its own type, and its border keeps the neighbors apart. The group draws no ring.
The count starts as a square of the avatar size and grows with the number, keeping its height and its text role.
The group is one image named by label, with the names and the total; the avatars and the count are not read.
claims.components-nph-badge-validation--matrix: Each severity value in both emphasis values, without an icon.
claims.components-nph-badge-validation--with-ic: The icon comes before the text, at icon/size-sm, in the text colour.
claims.components-nph-badge-validation--two-wor: One or two words stay on a single line: the badge does not wrap.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--matrix: Each severity and emphasis pair that exists, at the default size. Move the mouse over a button to see hover.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--sizes: The three sizes, with text and with an icon only. The text is label-md in all of them.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--icons: Start icon, end icon and both together, at icon/size-sm.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--disabl: Disabled: the whole button at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--loadin: Loading: the spinner takes the place of the start icon, and the text stays.
claims.components-nph-kbd-validation--single-ke: One key per piece, through the text property.
claims.components-nph-kbd-validation--combinati: A combination joins one piece per key, side by side.
claims.components-nph-kbd-validation--mac-combi: The same combination on macOS, with the system symbols. The application picks the set by the person's system; the piece does not detect it.
claims.components-nph-separator-validation--hor: Between stacked items, the line fills the width.
claims.components-nph-separator-validation--ver: Between side-by-side items, the line fills the height.
claims.components-nph-spinner-validation--sizes: sm inside a button or field; md in a content area.
claims.components-nph-spinner-validation--acces: With text beside it, the spinner is decorative; without text, it has an accessible name.
claims.components-nph-spinner-validation--inval: size="lg" does not exist: nothing is drawn, and the area below stays empty on purpose.
claims.components-nph-toggle-group-validation--: Two and three buttons, with text and icon only, in a group named by its subject; each button keeps its own state.
Single selection: it starts empty or with a value, checking one unchecks the others, and a click on the checked button does nothing.
Multiple selection: each button checks and unchecks on its own, and the value gathers the checked ones.
Disabled and invalid stay on each button: the group adds nothing, and the error message stays outside it.
A click changes the selection and fires nph-value-change with detail.value, shown below the group; setting value from code does not fire it.
The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: Alignment, Formatting and View.
claims.components-nph-togglebutton-validation--: Pressed off and on, valid and invalid, with text. Move the mouse over a button to see hover and press Tab to see focus.
Start and end icons: auto swaps xmark and check with the state, none draws no icon and a core name is one fixed icon.
Icon only: one icon, a label as the accessible name, 50 by 36 px and not square, side by side with one on.
Disabled: the whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order; disabled wins over invalid.
Invalid: the track border is status/error, pressed or not, with text or icon only; the message stays outside the piece.
A click toggles the piece and fires nph-change with detail.pressed, shown below the button; setting pressed from code does not fire it.
The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: Option off, Option on and Icon set.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--one-l: The open balloon above an element, with a one-line text, as in the Figma example.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--two-l: The open balloon with a two-line text: in every language it takes exactly two lines.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--sides: The four sides, top by default, with the action name of an icon-only button, in light and in dark mode.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--flip: The balloon flips to the opposite side when it does not fit on the preferred one.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--focus: Keyboard focus opens the balloon and Esc closes it, with the focus staying on the element.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--hover: Hover and keyboard focus open the balloon on any element: a button, a link and a field.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--matrix: Off and on, valid, invalid and disabled, with a label. Move the mouse over a piece to see hover and press Tab to see focus on the track.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--label: The label after the track; without text, only the track, named by label; a long label wraps to the available width, with the track at the top, aligned with the first line.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--disabl: Disabled: the whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order, on or off; disabled wins over invalid.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--invali: Invalid: the track outline is status/error, on or off, with a label or only the track; the error sentence stays outside the piece.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--intera: A click toggles the piece and fires the native input and change; checked is read from the target and shown below the piece. Setting checked from code fires nothing.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--exampl: The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: Single setting, Preferences and Unavailable setting.
